findings.title: Crowdsale._deliverTokens(address,uint256) ignores return value by token.transfer(_beneficiary,_tokenAmount)
findings.description: A token transfer's return value is ignored; a failed transfer passes silently. Slither: Crowdsale._deliverTokens(address,uint256) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#244-251) ignores return value by token.transfer(_beneficiary,_tokenAmount) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#250)

findings.title: Reentrancy in TemplateCrowdsale.init()
findings.description:
The function calls out to another contract before it finishes updating its own state. A malicious callee can re-enter while the state is half-written; no ether moves in the reentrant path itself, but the stale state can be abused. Slither: Reentrancy in TemplateCrowdsale.init() (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#1141-1166):
	External calls:
	- MainToken(token).pause() (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#1146)
	- MainToken(token).mint(addresses[i],amounts[i]) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#1156)
	- MainToken(token).mintAndFreeze(addresses[i],amounts[i],freezes[i]) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#1158)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- transferOwnership(TARGET_USER) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#1163)
		- owner = _newOwner (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#357)
	Ownable.owner (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#308) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- Ownable._transferOwnership(

findings.title: TimedCrowdsale.constructor(uint256,uint256) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.description:
Logic depends on block.timestamp, which miners can nudge by a few seconds (informational). Slither: TimedCrowdsale.constructor(uint256,uint256) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#386-393) uses timestamp for comparisons
	Dangerous comparisons:
	- require(bool)(_openingTime >= block.timestamp) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#388)
	- require(bool)(_closingTime >= _openingTime) (TemplateCrowdsale.sol#389)
